questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me that the country was an English speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had such a great time making new friends and studying interesting subjects not available at UCPH.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. The university sent a bunch of e-mails explaining what to do, and the website is useful as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to the reception of my accommodation to collect my keys, and there they would explain a little bit.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: People were really nice and helpfull.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were quite a lot of options. Both part-catered and self-catered, apartments and houses, shared bathrooms and en-suite bathrooms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my house we had a kitchen shared between five students. The kitchen was empty so you have to either bring kitchen equipment or buy it there. I was lucky to be able to borrow most things from my british housemates who brought a lot of stuff.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is so much fun and an easy way to quickly meet people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was pretty satisfied.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything was done online and explained by e-mail.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An Erasmus Team which helps you with administrative and practical matters before, during and after your time at the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I changed my classes during my stay.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don´t worry so much about it. The Erasmus Team will help you find a solution if you have any time clashes in your schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is generally high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had lectures and seminars just as we know it from UCPH. The seminar groups were generally smaller, which force students to engage more.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Human Rights Law in Context, International Law: Sources and Principles, Privacy, Data Protection and Cybersecurity Law and Asylum and Refugee Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend Privacy, Data Protection and Cybersecurity Law together with Asylum and Refugee Law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Shopping at the supermarkets on campus was more expensive than I expected, but the supermarkets in town were generally speaking less expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In freshers week there were a lot of fun activities: colour run, comedy shows, rave ping pong, speed friending, etc. Also, there is a bunch of sports available at University of Kent. New students even get a free membership to the gym on campus, which was really nice. Students can also visit the beautiful cathedral in town for free.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It is always a good idea to join one of the many sports available as they host socials once a week and just have a fun time together.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to Ramsgate, Dover, London and Paris (travelled with the Eurostar).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy as it is not that different from the Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say yes and go to a lot of social events on campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As a dane you will have to get used to their level of politeness. Remember to say "please" and "sorry" etc.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love how polite they are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remember to enjoy every second of your stay, go on trips with friends on the weekends and just have fun and don´t worry too much.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to travel buses and trains are available and to a pretty good prize if you book in advance. I would recommend National Express for buses and Trainline for trains.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting amazing people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably writing week when all your essays needed to be complete.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
